npc_godwin_porter.name: Godwin
npc_godwin_porter.look: A heavy, slow old porter in his late fifties with a broken nose, white stubble, a blue livery coat with the Ashby badge, a leather cap and a big ring of keys at his belt, leaning on a stout staff.
npc_godwin_porter.combat: slow and heavy, an old brawler
npc_godwin_porter.personality: Lazy, sharp-eyed and fond of a grievance; does the least he can, but knows exactly who is worth letting in. Soft on anyone who makes his day easier.
npc_godwin_porter.values: a quiet gate, his ale, his own judgement
npc_godwin_porter.fears: the steward's temper, trouble on his watch
npc_godwin_porter.authority: Keeps the manor gate and its keys.
npc_godwin_porter.concerns: The gate bell's rope snapped last night and he can't reach to mend it, so he's had to walk out to every caller himself. The steward's been shouting about the kitchen's kindling all morning.

steward.text: Steward Merrick decides who comes into the manor; he wants a reason and someone's word.
steward.line: The steward decides. He'll want a reason, and someone to vouch for you.
steward.lead: Steward Merrick admits people with a reason and someone's word for them.

ned.text: Ned the groom is the steward's favourite; a word from Ned goes a long way.
ned.line: Young Ned in the stables? Steward thinks the sun shines out of him.
ned.lead: Ned the groom has Steward Merrick's ear.

npc_godwin_porter.persuaded_by: anything that makes his day easier

samples: Bell's broke. So I have to walk. Again.
That's a kindness. Hm. Go on through, then.
Ask the steward. Not my place.
voice.habits: Jingles his keys; leans on his staff; grumbles about the bell.
voice.greeting: Squints through the gate: 'And who might you be?'

goals: Someone to mend the bell rope
npc_godwin_porter.likes: ale, sitting down, people who help

npc_merrick_steward.text: a hard master with his lists

superstition.text: Godwin would want to know how it works.

npc_godwin_porter.admits: Godwin lets through anyone the steward or Ned speaks for to his face, and anyone who does him or the house a real good turn he sees with his own eyes (like mending the gate bell). Never beggars or sweet talkers.

npc_merrick_steward.name: Merrick
npc_merrick_steward.look: A thin, precise man in his forties with a pointed grey beard, a dark green velvet doublet, a chain of office, a wax tablet and stylus in his hands, and a permanently worried frown.
npc_merrick_steward.personality: Precise, harried and fair; lives by lists and hates surprises. Admits anyone with a proper reason and a proper word for them.
npc_merrick_steward.values: order, the household's good name, his lists
npc_merrick_steward.fears: the lord's displeasure, thieves in the house
npc_merrick_steward.authority: Steward of Ashby Manor: decides who comes in.
npc_merrick_steward.concerns: Checking the delivery cart against his list. The kitchen has no kindling for the feast tonight and the lord's horse is off its feed.

feast.text: The lord holds a feast tonight; the house is short of hands.
feast.line: A feast tonight, and half the house laid up with a cough. We're short of hands.
feast.lead: Ashby Manor is short of hands for tonight's feast.

npc_merrick_steward.persuaded_by: a proper reason and a proper word, or proof of use

samples: Name. Business. Who vouches for you?
That is not on my list.
Ned says so? Hm. Ned is reliable.
voice.habits: Checks his tablet; taps the stylus; glances at the sky.
voice.never: admits someone on their own word
voice.greeting: Without looking up: 'If you're selling, go round the back.'

npc_ned_groom.text: the most reliable lad in the house

tasks.doing: checking the delivery cart against his list

superstition.text: Merrick would want to know how it works.

npc_merrick_steward.decides: Merrick admits anyone with a legitimate reason to come in (work for the house, business with it) and someone he trusts speaking for them to his face, or who has shown him with his own eyes that they're useful to the house.

npc_ned_groom.name: Ned
npc_ned_groom.look: A wiry, freckled youth of nineteen with tousled sandy hair, a leather jerkin over a striped shirt, riding breeches, straw on his boots and a horse brush in his hand.
npc_ned_groom.personality: Friendly, honest and eager to please; loves horses more than people and trusts anyone who's good with them.
npc_ned_groom.values: the horses, Steward Merrick's good opinion, fair dealing
npc_ned_groom.fears: the lord's horse falling sick, a scolding
npc_ned_groom.concerns: The lord's grey mare is off her feed, and her halter snapped this morning; he needs it mended before he can lead her out, and he's no hand with leather.

halter.text: The grey mare's halter snapped at the cheek strap; it wants new stitching.
halter.line: Her halter's gone at the cheek strap. Needs stitching, and I can't sew to save my life.
halter.lead: Ned the groom's halter needs its cheek strap stitched.

npc_ned_groom.persuaded_by: kindness to the horses, a job done
npc_ned_groom.style: Quick and friendly; talks to the horses mid-sentence.

samples: Are you any good with leather?
Mend that and I'll speak to the steward for you myself.
The steward listens to me. Mostly.
voice.habits: Brushes a horse while talking; whistles; blushes.
voice.greeting: Looks up from brushing: 'Morning! You lost?'

superstition.text: Ned would want to know how it works.

offers.task: stitch the grey mare's broken halter
offers.check: Has the stranger mended Ned's halter?
